diagnostic_evidence.quote: $A_\omega$ is defined for any $\omega \in [0,1]$ and is continuous with respect to $\omega$ there.

issues.failure_explanation: The example claims that continuity of d suffices for the binary Fréchet mean to satisfy all five average axioms. Every metric is continuous in its arguments, so the hypothesis is vacuous; but in a general metric space the minimizer may fail to exist or to be unique (so A_ω is not a well-defined map Ω×Ω→Ω), and ω ↦ A_ω may be discontinuous, violating item 1 of Definition def:average. Concrete counterexample: the three-point space {x,y,z} with the discrete metric gives A_ω(x,y) = x for ω < 1/2 and A_ω(x,y) = y for ω > 1/2 with a tie at ω = 1/2, so the Fréchet mean is neither single-valued nor continuous in ω. The claim holds only under substantial extra structure (e.g., NPC/CAT(0) spaces, where the minimizer exists, is unique, and coincides with the geodesic average), not from continuity of d alone.

failure_location.quote: It is easy to verify that if the metric $d$ is continuous as a function of its arguments, then the binary Fr\'echet mean satisfies all the requirements of Definition~\ref{def:average}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the assertion to metric spaces in which the two-point Fréchet mean exists, is unique, and is continuous in ω (e.g., NPC/CAT(0) spaces), or add equivalent hypotheses; the claim cannot stand under continuity of d alone.
issues.overall_effect: Only this illustrative example is affected; no definition, theorem, or later example relies on it, but as stated it misinforms the reader about when Fréchet means furnish averages.
issues.title: Fréchet mean asserted to be an average assuming only continuity of the metric
issues.why_classification: A local, illustrative false claim with no dependents; adding the standard NPC/uniqueness hypothesis or deleting the sentence preserves every substantive claim of the paper.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Given is a sequence $\PP  \in \Omega^\Z $ associated with a sequence $T = \{ t_j \}_{j \in \Z} \in \R^\Z$ of parameters, where $t_j < t_{j+1}$, for all $j \in \Z$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem (and the limit-curve definition with the metric d_∞ over t ∈ ℝ) asserts a limit curve defined on all of ℝ, and the proof covers ℝ by intervals [t^{k+1}_{2j}, t^{k+1}_{2j+2}). But the definitions require only strictly increasing parameter sequences, and conditions (3.1)-(3.2) preserve the parameter range: if T^0 is bounded (e.g., t^0_j = arctan(j)), then every piecewise average interpolant is defined only on a bounded interval, the intervals do not cover ℝ, and both Q^∞(t) for t ∈ ℝ and d_∞ are undefined. The proof thus needs, but never states, that the parameter sequences are unbounded above and below (t_j → ±∞).

failure_location.quote: then it converges to a continuous limit $Q^\infty(t) \in \Omega$, $t \in \R $, from any initial data $Q^0 = (T^0,\PP^0)$ with $\PP^0 \in \D$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to Definition def:refinement (or to the convergence results) the standing requirement that parameter sequences satisfy t_j → +∞ and t_j → -∞; this holds for the primal and dual parameterizations and every example in the paper.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the conclusions of Theorems thm:convergence, thm:main_proximity, thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType and thm:C1_m1 (and transitively thm:C1_manifold) are ill-defined for bounded parameter rules. All examples and applications use the primal or dual parameterizations, which satisfy the missing hypothesis, so they are unaffected once it is added.
issues.title: No hypothesis ensures parameter sequences cover ℝ, yet limit curves are claimed on all of ℝ
issues.why_classification: An omitted standard hypothesis that is satisfied by every parameterization the paper actually uses; adding it changes no method, conclusion, or application.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound (3.9) of the third term of (3.8) rests on the inclusion [t^{k+1}_{2j}, t^{k+1}_{2j+2}) ⊂ [t^k_j, t^k_{j+1}), claimed to follow from (3.1). But (3.1) places t^{k+1}_{2j+2} in [t^k_{j+1}, t^k_{j+2}), so the inclusion holds only when t^{k+1}_{2j+2} = t^k_{j+1} (as in the primal parameterization). For the dual parameterization discussed in Section 2, t^{k+1}_{2j+2} = t^k_{j+1} + 2^{-(k+2)} > t^k_{j+1}, so t ∈ [t^k_{j+1}, t^{k+1}_{2j+2}) lies in the next interval [t^k_{j+1}, t^k_{j+2}) and the bound d(S^k(P)_j, PA(Q^k;t)) ≤ δ(S^k(P)) is false; the correct bound is 2δ(S^k(P)) (add d(p^k_j, p^k_{j+1})). The same one-off factor appears in Theorem thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType's bound d(PA(Q^{ℓ+ν};t), S_1^{ℓ+ν}(P)_{2^ν j}) ≤ 2^ν δ at ν = 0, which should likewise be 2δ.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the third-term bound by d(S^k(P)_j, PA(Q^k;t)) ≤ 2δ(S^k(P)) via d(p^k_j,p^k_{j+1}) + d(p^k_{j+1}, PA(Q^k;t)), and correspondingly use 2δ (not 2^ν δ with factor 1 at ν = 0) in the proof of thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType; only constants in the estimates change.
issues.overall_effect: The Cauchy estimate in the proof of Theorem thm:convergence (and the analogous step in Theorem thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType, inherited by thm:C1_m1) is incorrect as written for non-primal parameterizations such as the dual one; the statements of these results survive with a larger constant in the final geometric bound.
issues.title: False cross-level interval inclusion in the main convergence proof
issues.why_classification: A localized false inference with a routine one-line repair (an extra triangle-inequality step) that leaves every conclusion and rate intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $S$ be a subdivision scheme, and let $\D\subset \Omega^\Z$, such that if $\PP \in \D$, then $S(\PP) \in \D$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes contraction of W only along levels that are multiples of L (equation (5.4): δ(W^{kL}P) ≤ μ_W^k δ(P) when δ(P) ≤ ν), and then invokes Theorem thm:convergence. That theorem requires a domain D' with W(D') ⊂ D' on which W^L is contractive. The natural choice D' = {P ∈ D : δ(P) ≤ ν} is invariant under W^L by (5.4) but is not shown to be invariant under W: no hypothesis controls δ(W^r P) for 1 ≤ r < L, since D-S bounds only even-index displacement and proximity bounds only W^L. Consequently the repeated contractivity used in Theorem thm:convergence's proof (equation (3.7)) is unavailable at levels not divisible by L, and for L ≥ 2 the convergence of W is not established. For L = 1 the induction (5.4) already covers every level, so the argument is complete in that case.

failure_location.quote: Finally, the weak convergence of the scheme $W$ follows by Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence} since $W$ has a contractivity factor when $\delta(\PP)$ is small enough, it is D-S in $\D$, and it maps $\D$ onto itself.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a one-step boundedness hypothesis δ(W(P)) ≤ K δ(P) for P ∈ D (equivalently strengthen D-S to all indices, or assume the sublevel set {δ ≤ ν} ∩ D is W-invariant, or assume one-step proximity between S and W); then (5.4) extends to all residue classes modulo L with the bound (5.3) divided by a constant depending on K and L, and Theorem thm:convergence applies.
issues.overall_effect: For contractivity number L ≥ 2 the weak convergence of W, the explicit density bound (5.3), and the remark that μ_W can be made close to μ are unproven as stated. The paper's application in Corollary cor:added-1 uses L = 1 and is unaffected.
issues.title: First-type proximity theorem applies the convergence theorem outside its hypotheses for L ≥ 2
issues.why_classification: The final appeal to Theorem thm:convergence is invalid as written, and repair requires a genuinely new (though standard) hypothesis plus a worsened constant in the advertised density bound; the theorem's form and its L = 1 application survive, so no new proof architecture or major loss results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType} does not rely on a contractivity factor of $S_1$ and so we do not require $S_1$ to have the D-S property.
The subdivision scheme $S_1^L$ is in proximity of the second type of order $m=0$  to $S_2^L$ in $\D$.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound of the middle term in (6.7) uses displacement-safety of S_1, but the theorem's three hypotheses do not include it, and Remark rem:prox_2 explicitly states that D-S of S_1 is not required. Without some displacement control the theorem is false. Counterexample: in Ω = ℝ with the arithmetic average, take S_1 = S_2 = S with S(P)_{2j} = p_j + c and S(P)_{2j+1} = (p_j + p_{j+1})/2 + c for a fixed c > 0. S is a local refinement operator; the shift cancels in consecutive differences, so δ(S(P)) = δ(P)/2 and S_2 is contractive with μ = 1/2, L = 1 on D = ℝ^ℤ, which S_1 preserves; S_1^L = S_2^L trivially satisfies order-0 second-type proximity (the schemes coincide); both use the primal parameterization. Yet the piecewise interpolants satisfy f^k(t) = f^0(t) + kc, so d_∞(f^{k+1}, f^k) = c and there is no limit: the conclusion fails although every stated hypothesis holds. The same example shows that a contractive S_2 need not itself converge without a displacement condition.

failure_location.quote: The middle term on the RHS of~\eqref{eqn:W_proof_main} is bounded by $C_{S_1} \delta (S_1^{\ell} (\PP))$ since $S_1$ is D-S.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add 'S_1 is displacement-safe in D' to the hypotheses (the proof already uses it at eqn:W_middleterm), correct Remark rem:prox_2 accordingly, and keep the rest of the proof; the scheme in Theorem thm:C1_manifold satisfies d(S(P)_{2j}, p_j) ≤ (ω/2) δ(P), so the applications are preserved.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType is false as stated, and Remark rem:prox_2's justification for dropping D-S is false. The theorem is used for the convergence part of Theorem thm:C1_m1 and hence for Theorem thm:C1_manifold. After adding the D-S hypothesis, the strong-convergence guarantee and the applications (whose schemes are D-S) stand.
issues.title: Second-type convergence theorem's proof uses D-S of S_1, which is not a hypothesis; the theorem is false without it
issues.why_classification: The stated theorem admits an explicit counterexample, but the least repair is the limited weakening of adding exactly the hypothesis the proof already uses; the central guarantee (strong convergence from any initial data) and all applications survive, with only the advertised 'no D-S needed' advantage withdrawn.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \[ \sup_{i \in \Z} d\left( S_1^L( S_1^{jL}(\PP))_i,S_2^L( S_1^{jL}(\PP))_i \right) \le E \eta^{j+1} , \quad \eta < \left( \frac{1}{2} \right)^{m} ,\quad j \in \Z_+ . \]

issues.failure_explanation: As restated before the theorem, proximity of S_1^L to S_2^L yields the bound E η^{j+1} only at levels jL (sequences S_1^{jL}P). In the recursion (6.4) the bound is used at Q = S_1^{ℓ-L}P for arbitrary ℓ with exponent ℓ-L+1; what the hypothesis actually provides there is E_r η^{⌊ℓ/L⌋} with a constant E_r depending on the residue orbit S_1^r P (r = ℓ mod L). Since η < 1 and ℓ-L+1 ≥ ⌊ℓ/L⌋ (with equality only for L = 1), the displayed recursion uses a stronger decay than justified. With the corrected exponent and E = max_r E_r, the same iteration gives Σ_{s<q} μ^s η^{q-s} ≤ q α^q, so the final bound (6.5) and the theorem (once the D-S hypothesis of the preceding issue is added) are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the proximity term by E η^{⌊ℓ/L⌋} with E = max_{0 ≤ r < L} E(S_1^r P) (allowed since E may depend on P) and carry the corrected exponent through the iteration; the form of (6.5) is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Only the intermediate display eqn:delta_S1P is unjustified; the conclusion of Theorem thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType is preserved after a routine exponent correction. (The same misuse is consequential in Theorem thm:C1_m1 and is reported separately.)
issues.title: Proximity decay used with a per-level exponent that the stated hypothesis does not provide
issues.why_classification: A local unjustified step whose forced correction (correct exponent and maximal constant) leaves the final estimate and the statement intact.

issues.failure_explanation: Applied to the pair (S_1^{L_1}, S_2^{L_1}), Definition def:2nd_type_prox_def provides sup_i ||S_1^{L_1}(S_1^{jL_1}P)_i - S_2^{L_1}(S_1^{jL_1}P)_i|| ≤ E η^{j+1} with η < (1/2)^1 = 1/2, i.e., a bound at every L_1-th refinement level (per-refinement decay η^{1/L_1}). The proof instead uses the bound E η^{ℓ-L_1+1} at every level ℓ. With the correct exponent, the perturbation in the recursion for a_ℓ = δ(Δ(S_1^ℓ P)/2^{-ℓ}) is 2^{ℓ+1} E η^{⌊ℓ/L_1⌋} = Θ((2^{L_1} η)^{⌊ℓ/L_1⌋}), which decays only when η < 2^{-L_1}. For L_1 ≥ 2 this is not implied by η < 1/2 (e.g., η = 0.4, L_1 = 2 gives factor 2^{L_1}η = 1.6 > 1), so the divided differences need not contract and the C^1 conclusion is unproven in that regime.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the order-m proximity requirement for L-step powers to η < 2^{-mL} (equivalently, require sup_i d(S_1^L(S_1^j P)_i, S_2^L(S_1^j P)_i) ≤ E η^{j+1} at every refinement level j), or add the hypothesis η < 2^{-L_1} to Theorem thm:C1_m1; the difference recursion then contracts as needed.
issues.overall_effect: For L_1 ≥ 2 and η ∈ [2^{-L_1}, 1/2) the C^1 conclusion of Theorem thm:C1_m1 is unsupported; the advertised link 'order 1 second-type proximity implies C^1' survives only under a strengthened threshold. The application in Theorem thm:C1_manifold uses L_1 = 1 with η = 1/4 and is unaffected.
issues.title: Order-1 proximity with η < 1/2 does not make divided differences contract when L_1 ≥ 2
issues.why_classification: The proof's decay inference fails under the stated hypothesis for L_1 ≥ 2; the repair narrows the proximity regime (or strengthens the hypothesis) but preserves the order-smoothness framework and the paper's L_1 = 1 application.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: It is worth noting that a subdivision scheme $S$ with a first-order contractivity factor, which also satisfies the D-S property, is $C^1$.

issues.failure_explanation: To conclude that the divided differences D^ℓ = Δ(S_1^ℓ P)/2^{-ℓ} yield a Cauchy sequence of interpolants, the proof transplants Theorem thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType's three-term estimate. There the middle term is bounded by the D-S property of the refined sequence (eqn:W_middleterm); for the divided-difference sequence the analogous term is ||D^{ℓ+1}_{2j} - D^ℓ_j||, a cross-level displacement of divided differences that no hypothesis bounds: D^ℓ is not an orbit of a subdivision scheme to which proximity applies, D-S of S_1 (even once added) constrains point displacement rather than divided-difference displacement, and only L_1-step order-1 proximity is assumed, which says nothing about one-step divided-difference displacement. For linear schemes this term is bounded by the difference scheme's D-S property, but S_1 and S_2 are allowed to be nonlinear, so the Cauchy property — the heart of the C^1 claim — is not established. The same gap underlies the unlabelled remark after Definition def:more asserting that first-order contractivity plus D-S implies C^1, which the cited reference justifies only for linear schemes.

failure_location.quote:
Thus, the rest of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType} is valid for 
\[ Q^\ell=\{(t_j^\ell,(\Delta (S_1^\ell (\PP)) / 2^{-\ell})_j\}_{j\in \Z}, \]
namely, it is a Cauchy sequence.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the classical C^1-proximity hypotheses: one-step order-1 proximity between S_1 and S_2 and displacement-safety of S_2's difference scheme (automatic for linear S_2 reproducing linear functions); then ||D^{ℓ+1}_{2j} - D^ℓ_j|| splits into a proximity term O((2η)^ℓ) and a difference-scheme D-S term O(δ(D^ℓ)), both summable. This covers the application, where S_2 = S_lin is linear.
issues.overall_effect: The C^1 conclusion of Theorem thm:C1_m1 is unproven for nonlinear schemes as stated; Theorem thm:C1_manifold, which is reduced to thm:C1_m1, depends on the repaired statement, and the motivational claim after Definition def:more is unsupported beyond the linear case.
issues.title: No cross-level displacement bound for divided differences in the C^1 argument
issues.why_classification: A necessary nontrivial step is missing from the C^1 proof; the repair adds standard hypotheses that hold in the paper's application and keeps the same proof architecture and conclusion type, so the result survives in recognizably comparable form.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $S_2$ be a subdivision scheme defined on $\R^n$ that satisfies~\eqref{eqn:contractivity_diff} with a contractivity factor $\mudelta$ and a contractivity number $L_1$ in $\D \subset \big( \R^n \big)^\Z$.
and such that there exists $\D \subset \Omega^\Z$ where $S_2$ has a contractivity factor $\mu\in (0,1)$ and a contractivity number $L\in \N$.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType requires S_2 to be zero-order contractive in the sense of Definition def:contractivity (δ(S_2^L Q) ≤ μ δ(Q)), but Theorem thm:C1_m1 assumes only the first-order contractivity (6.10) of S_2, which contracts scaled second differences. For a general nonlinear S_2 the former is not a consequence of the latter, and δ(D^ℓ) → 0 does not bound ||D^ℓ||_∞, so convergence of S_1 cannot be recovered from the first-order analysis alone; in addition, once the missing D-S hypothesis of thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType is restored, thm:C1_m1 does not assume D-S of S_1 either. The paper's own Conjecture correctly includes contractivity of all orders n = 0,...,m, indicating the intended hypothesis.

failure_location.quote: Moreover, the convergence of $S_1$ is guaranteed by Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType} since $S_2$ is contractive and proximity of order $m=1$ implies proximity of order $m=0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add zero-order contractivity of S_2 in D (as the Conjecture assumes for n = 0,...,m) and displacement-safety of S_1 to the hypotheses of Theorem thm:C1_m1; then thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType applies since order-1 proximity implies order-0 proximity.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence assertion within Theorem thm:C1_m1 is unsupported for S_2 satisfying only (6.10); Theorem thm:C1_manifold cites thm:C1_m1 and is affected, although its S_2 = S_lin is a convergent (hence zero-order contractive) linear scheme and its S_1 is D-S, so the application is rescued by the repair.
issues.title: C^1 theorem cites the convergence theorem without zero-order contractivity of S_2
issues.why_classification: The cited theorem is used outside its hypotheses; the repair adds a hypothesis present in the paper's own Conjecture and satisfied in the application, leaving a recognizably comparable result, but the class of admissible nonlinear S_2 shrinks.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lemma:dist bounds ||A_ω(x,y) - ((1-ω)x + ωy)||. In the displayed computation, y = A_{1/2}(p_j,p_{j+1}) is the geodesic midpoint, but the subtracted convex combination uses the Euclidean midpoint (p_j+p_{j+1})/2, so the lemma does not apply to the written expression; the next line then replaces ||p_j - A_{1/2}(p_j,p_{j+1})|| by (1/2)||p_j - p_{j+1}||, which is valid for the Euclidean midpoint but false for the geodesic midpoint in general (e.g., near-antipodal points on a sphere, where the geodesic midpoint can be much farther from p_j than half the chord). The correct estimate needs the extra midpoint-comparison term ω||A_{1/2}(p_j,p_{j+1}) - (p_j+p_{j+1})/2||, which is O(||p_j-p_{j+1}||²) by the same lemma at ω = 1/2, so the final O(δ(P^ℓ)²) bound survives. Separately, the chain gives (2C)(1/4)((1/2)^ℓ δ(P^0))² = 2C δ(P^0)² (1/4)^{ℓ+1}, so the identified constant E = 2C δ(P^0) drops a square; this does not affect the proximity, whose constant may depend on P.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply Lemma lemma:dist with y = A_{1/2}(p_j,p_{j+1}) on both sides and insert the midpoint-comparison term ω||A_{1/2}(p_j,p_{j+1}) - (p_j+p_{j+1})/2|| (bounded via the same lemma at ω = 1/2); set E = 2C δ(P^0)².
issues.overall_effect: Two incorrect steps in the verification of order-1 proximity in Lemma lem:added-1; the lemma's conclusion (proximity with η = 1/4 and some constant E depending on P) remains valid after the routine corrections, so Theorem thm:C1_manifold is not further affected by this defect.
issues.title: Misapplication of the geodesic-versus-chord lemma and dropped square in the proximity constant for the manifold example
issues.why_classification: The defective steps are local and the forced corrections use only the already-cited lemma; the lemma's conclusion and everything downstream are unchanged.
